title: A connectome rate model of the larval zebrafish eye-position integrator did not predict where imaged cells are sensitive and gave the opposite sign for the sensitivity-persistence relation
abstract: We tested the published connectome rate model of the larval zebrafish hindbrain eye-position integrator (Vishwanathan et al. 2024) beyond the population distributions that it was shown to match. The EM wiring comes from one fish. Calcium-imaging data come from 20 other fish. Both are registered to the Z-brain atlas. In the overlap region (39 EM integrator somas, 177 imaged integrator cells), model sensitivity did not predict the local imaging sensitivity (Spearman rho -0.17, 95% CI -0.48 to 0.33). It was not positive in any of eight variants. Imaged sensitivity increased with depth; the model depth slope was negative or uncertain. Model and imaging persistence maps agreed weakly (rho +0.30, CI -0.10 to 0.60), but shuffles that kept the two oculomotor submodules gave the same value. In an exploratory test that needs no registration, model cells with higher sensitivity had more persistent activity (rho +0.82; all 600 degree-preserving wiring shuffles stayed positive, minimum +0.46). Imaged cells with higher sensitivity had less persistent activity (rho -0.28, CI -0.36 to -0.20, n 584). This sign held for later windows, in each depth quartile and without ramping cells. The model predicts 3.4 times higher sensitivity for abducens internuclear than motor neurons; eight imaged internuclear cells were not clearly more sensitive. Limitations: one EM animal, no fish identifiers in the imaging files, a small overlap region, unknown registration error and calcium-indicator kinetics. The 178 EM cells without somas in the volume were excluded from the primary spatial test. Code, aggregate results and figures are included; external data stay outside the bundle with a pinned retrieval script and hashes.

display.caption: Sensitivity-persistence relation. A: median post-saccade decay ratio (5.3-6 s over 2.3-3 s) by sensitivity quintile, imaging integrator cells (blue, n 585) and connectome-model oculomotor cells (orange, n 255); bars are bootstrap 95% intervals of the median. B: Spearman rho between sensitivity and decay ratio for three window pairs (imaging with bootstrap CI; model with random positive input), and 95% ranges of 200 wiring shuffles each (1, 2, 7 blocks, published input, main window). The signs are opposite.

Spatial tests, soma-only primary analysis. A: coverage of imaged integrator cells and EM integrator somas in Z-brain space. B, C: standardised rank slopes of sensitivity and persistence on rostro-caudal, lateral and depth coordinates in the overlap region (bootstrap 95% CI) with shuffle 95% ranges. D: map agreement between model values and local imaging means with shuffle ranges. E: sensitivity percentile by depth. F: abducens sensitivity relative to integrator cells, model versus imaging.
